definitions.explanation: Acting on one's own initiative without being directed or compelled by others. Used as a modifier to describe activities, organizations, or decisions made independently.

examples.japanese: {自主|じしゅ}{練習|れんしゅう}に{励|はげ}む。
examples.english: To work hard at independent practice.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{製品|せいひん}の{自主|じしゅ}{回収|かいしゅう}を{決|き}めた。
examples.english: The company decided on a voluntary recall of the product.

examples.japanese: {生徒|せいと}たちが{自主的|じしゅてき}に{校庭|こうてい}の{清掃|せいそう}{活動|かつどう}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: The students voluntarily carried out a cleanup of the schoolyard.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used as a modifier: {自主|じしゅ}～ (noun compound) or {自主的|じしゅてき}に (adverbial). Implies initiative and self-motivation. In Japanese society, {自主|じしゅ} actions are generally viewed positively as showing maturity and responsibility.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自主|じしゅ}{練習|れんしゅう}: independent practice
- {自主|じしゅ}{回収|かいしゅう}: voluntary recall
- {自主|じしゅ}{規制|きせい}: voluntary regulation, self-censorship
- {自主的|じしゅてき}に: voluntarily, on one's own initiative
- {自主|じしゅ}{退職|たいしょく}: voluntary resignation
- {自主|じしゅ}{制作|せいさく}: independent production
